policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: All three readings contain the same words; they differ only in where the appositional clause sits and in punctuation. ASV 'the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy' is the ordinary English arrangement of either order, so the English does not distinguish them.
Pure word order of the same two words; ASV 'hath power' renders either. The note is alternative_rendering ('Or, authority') about English wording only.
Plural vs singular of the same verb with a neuter-plural subject; ASV 'Are not five sparrows sold' is the required English for both.
Presence or absence of the connective oun. ASV 'Fear not' carries no 'therefore', but ASV routinely leaves an inferential particle unrendered, so its absence does not settle the Greek.
Aorist subjunctive vs future indicative of the same verb in a relative clause; ASV 'whosoever shall confess' (Every one who shall confess) renders either.
Compounds of phero that both mean bring in/bring before; ASV 'when they bring you before the synagogues' does not distinguish the prefix.
Aorist subjunctive vs present imperative prohibition of the same verb; both are 'be not anxious' in English.
ASV 'be not anxious how or what ye shall answer' renders the words e ti alongside pos; the omitting reading would leave only 'how ye shall answer'.
Word order of the same words; ASV 'And one out of the multitude said unto him' fits either.
Two synonyms for judge; ASV 'a judge or a divider' renders either.
ASV 'keep yourselves from all covetousness' renders pases; the variant reads only the article and would give 'from covetousness'. ASV renders pas consistently as 'all'.
Genitive vs dative of the same pronoun in the clause about a man's abundance; neither the ASV text nor its alternative_rendering note distinguishes the case.
Dative vs genitive of the same pronoun; ASV 'a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth' renders either construal, and the note is alternative_rendering only.
Orthographic variants of the same reflexive pronoun; ASV 'within himself' is identical for both.
ASV 'there will I bestow all my grain and my goods' renders ton siton (grain); the variant ta genemata mou would give produce/fruits, which ASV uses in v.17 for a different word.
Two vocative forms of the same adjective; ASV 'Thou foolish one' renders either.
Simplex vs compound of the same verb, both 'ask/require'; ASV 'is thy soul required of thee' and the gloss 'Greek they require thy soul' fit both.
Orthographic variants of the same reflexive pronoun; ASV 'for himself' is identical for both.
Word order of the same two words; ASV 'I say unto you' renders either.

ASV 'for your life' has 'your', but English idiom requires a possessive here and ASV supplies one at 'your body' too, where the base has no pronoun. The possessive therefore does not show whether humon stood with psyche.
Same situation as the preceding unit: ASV 'nor yet for your body' supplies the idiomatic possessive in both halves of the verse, so it does not attest humon after somati.
ASV opens the verse 'For the life is more than the food', rendering the causal gar that the variant omits.
Word order only: whether the infinitive precedes or follows the prepositional phrase. ASV 'can add a cubit unto the measure of his life' follows English order either way.
Presence of hena with pechyn. ASV 'a cubit' uses the indefinite article, which is an ordinary rendering of both an anarthrous noun and hena, so the English does not settle it.
Orthographic variants (oude / oute) of the same negative; ASV 'ye are not able to do even that which is least' renders either.
Word order and the article with agro; ASV 'the grass in the field, which to-day is' requires the English article regardless, and all three orders yield the same clause.
Two present forms of the same verb 'clothe'; ASV 'doth so clothe' renders either.
ASV 'what ye shall eat, and what ye shall drink' renders kai; the variant e would give 'or', which ASV distinguishes from 'and'.
Plural vs singular verb with the neuter-plural subject ta ethne; ASV 'do the nations of the world seek after' is the required English for both.
ASV text reads 'his kingdom' (autou), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read the kingdom of God' places the tou theou reading in the margin, not the text.
ASV 'and these things shall be added unto you' has no 'all'; ASV renders panta as 'all' wherever it stands, so the addition is excluded.

ASV 'if he shall come in the second watch, and if in the third' supplies 'come' and 'watch' with the first clause, but both words stand later in the base clause too; the English order does not show whether they were repeated with the second watch.

ASV 'blessed are those servants' has the noun the variant adds, but 'those' alone needs an English noun and ASV has 'those servants' in v.37 where the Greek supplies it; the render shows no italics either way, so the noun does not settle the Greek.

ASV 'he would have watched, and not have left his house' renders egregoresen an kai, which the base lacks entirely; that excludes r00. The two remaining readings differ only in a second an, which the English cannot show.
Two aorist passive forms of the same verb; ASV 'to be broken through' with the gloss 'Greek digged through' renders either.
Presence or absence of oun. ASV 'Be ye also ready' carries no 'therefore', but ASV frequently leaves the particle unrendered, so its absence does not decide the reading.
ASV 'And Peter said, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us' has no indirect object; ASV renders an explicit auto in a speech formula as 'unto him', so the addition is excluded.
kai eipen vs eipen de; ASV renders both connectives 'And', and 'And the Lord said' fits either.

Repeated article vs kai before phronimos. ASV 'the faithful and wise steward' is an ordinary rendering of both, and the second construal appears only in a note classed alternative_rendering, which cannot decide a reading.
Presence or absence of the article with sitometrion; ASV 'their portion of food' requires no article distinction in English.
Possessive vs reflexive pronoun for the same referent; ASV 'his lord's will' renders either.
e vs mede joining the participles after a negative; ASV 'and made not ready, nor did according to his will' is the natural English for both.
epi vs eis with ten gen after 'cast'; ASV 'to cast fire upon the earth' renders either preposition in this idiom, and the note is alternative_rendering about the following clause.
Two forms of the relative in the temporal phrase heos hotou / heos hou; ASV 'till it be accomplished' renders either.
Word order of the same two words; ASV 'five in one house divided' renders either.
ASV opens 'They shall be divided, father against son', a plural verb standing before the paired subjects; the singular variant would give 'Father shall be divided against son'.
Presence or absence of the article with thygatera; ASV 'mother against daughter' shows no article either way.
Accusative with epi vs dative; ASV 'mother against daughter' renders either case.
Articular accusative vs dative of meter; ASV 'daughter against her mother' renders either, the possessive being an English supply.

Addition of autes after pentheran. ASV 'daughter in law against her mother in law' has 'her', but ASV supplies the same possessive at 'against her mother' earlier in the verse where no pronoun stands, so it does not attest autes.

Presence or absence of the article with nephelen; ASV 'a cloud rising in the west' uses the indefinite article, which English idiom permits for the articular Greek here as well, so the reading is not settled.
ASV 'rising in the west' renders epi dysmon; apo dysmon would be 'out of the west', and ASV distinguishes 'in' from 'from/out of' in rendering these prepositions.
Recitative hoti before direct speech; ASV 'ye say, There cometh a shower' leaves it untranslated as English requires, so its presence cannot be seen.
Position of the postpositive de relative to kairon; ASV 'but how is it that ye know not how to interpret this time' renders either order.
ASV 'ye know not how to interpret this time' renders ouk oidate with the infinitive dokimazein; the variant ou dokimazete would give simply 'ye interpret not'.
Future indicative vs aorist subjunctive after mepote; ASV 'and the judge shall deliver thee to the officer' renders either.
Future indicative vs aorist subjunctive of ballo in the same clause chain; ASV 'shall cast thee into prison' renders either.
heos kai to vs heos hou kai ton: a relative added to the conjunction and the gender of the article with lepton. ASV 'till thou have paid the very last mite' shows neither.
